answer: One concrete Sybil defence is a stake-plus-slash gate: every agent identity must lock a real bond before it may attest, and the bond burns if its votes diverge from the attested majority over a window. A fake swarm therefore faces a river of separately paid tributaries rather than one free signature, since cloning a thousand agents costs a thousand full bonds plus idle-capital cost. Each clone earns slow umber-grade income only from steady honest work. That linear cost makes an island of a few funded real actors cheaper than a mainland of fakes.
